name: pdk-rafiki-cached-introspection-revocation
instr:
# Cache GNAP introspection without stale authorizations

Every Open Payments request currently introspects its GNAP token at auth. Cache token validations in the backend so unchanged, previously validated tokens can be reused when introspection is temporarily unavailable. Services share state only through Redis and their databases, not local files.

What we need:
- For 20 sequential reads on one instance, send no more than one introspection request; after 20 reads on a second instance, no more than two in total.
- An acknowledged token revocation, rotation, client grant cancellation or admin grant revocation rejects every old token on both instances. The replacement token after rotation remains usable. A revoked token cannot re-enter a cache via an in-flight validation or a replica that lost Redis connectivity. A committed grant revocation survives auth crashing before publication; auth cannot report healthy after restart until its committed revocations are effective. Do not install database triggers or rules on the `grants` table.
- Cached validation is scoped to token, wallet address, resource type and action. A token valid for reading one incoming payment cannot create payments or access another wallet. Cached tokens stop working at their expiry, as reported by auth introspection. New tokens are not admitted while auth is unavailable; previously validated, unexpired, unrevoked tokens remain usable.
